set.body:
Fixture

Use 48-72 trials over at least two runs, two stimulus classes, three load levels, match/mismatch probes, variable 4-10 second delays, continuous RT with declared missingness, fractional onsets, and overlapping phase responses.

Required design

- Sample: stimulus class x one canonical basis = 2 columns.
- Delay: load x eight FIR bins = 24 columns.
- Probe: match status x load x canonical-plus-temporal-derivative = 12 columns.
- Probe RT slopes: centered within match-status x load cells, ZeroContribution missing policy, same informed basis = 12 columns.
- Total task columns before intercept/drift/nuisance terms = exactly 50.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The structural schema proves the 2 + 24 + 12 + 12 count and every origin before fitting.
- [ ] Planted effects include sample stimulus difference, monotonic delay load effect, probe mismatch effect, match-by-load interaction, mismatch-specific RT slope, and a modest temporal shift.
- [ ] Hypotheses cover sample response mean at 4-8s, delay linear trend over a FIR window, probe mismatch at 6s, match-by-load response interaction, RT slope difference, noncanonical probe omnibus, and delay FIR omnibus.
- [ ] An intentionally empty cell produces a declared non-estimable hypothesis and useful rank/alias evidence.
- [ ] Response data are generated from an independent checked-in/slow continuous-time oracle, not the design compiler being tested.
- [ ] The public construction performs no manual table explosion, basis-column offsets, integer contrast vectors, label parsing, or external centering.
- [ ] Numerical, structural, audit, provenance, and hypothesis results are all asserted.
- [ ] The scenario is registered with receipts, runs on JVM and Scala.js, and is published as executable documentation.
set.title: P3.2: add the 50-column delayed-match-to-sample acceptance scenario
